answer: Filling 83 aliases thus means producing 83 separate sets of claims, which is authoring work rather than a lookup. Because the ivory count is verified against the glacier text itself, the island audit records each rejection and the operator cannot amortise one paragraph. An answer claiming a deep mechanism must supply at least 6 distinct supporting claims, and the count is checked before grading so shallow text cannot pass by padding. That is 8 dollars per alias. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
